reason: Hypothesis A directly addresses hot-cracking in a non-weldable superalloy (IN738LC) with a physically sound mechanism (reduced thermal gradients and low-melting phase segregation) supported by specific, directly relevant evidence (E1–E3), and proposes a clear, testable falsification experiment. Hypothesis B relies on evidence from a different material system (H13 steel) and alloy (Inconel 718) without demonstrating applicability to the cast Inconel 713C, and its mechanism for mitigating hot cracking is less well-grounded for the stated material and conditions.
